description: Queries where context lacks sufficient evidence for confident answers - system should mark as QUALIFIED
mode_rationale: QUALIFIED because context provides partial/uncertain evidence. System should answer with appropriate hedging (correlation vs causation, limited sample, etc.).

cases.query: Why did employee satisfaction decrease?
contexts: Employee satisfaction scores dropped from 4.2 to 3.1 on a 5-point scale over the past year.
During this period, the company implemented a return-to-office policy and restructured several departments.
Exit interviews mentioned concerns about work-life balance and career growth opportunities.
cases.description: Correlating events but no confirmed causal link
cases.rationale: Multiple events occurred - can't definitively attribute satisfaction drop to any single cause

cases.query: What impact will AI have on employment?
contexts: McKinsey estimates 30% of work activities could be automated by 2030.
Historical automation has created more jobs than it eliminated, though in different sectors.
Current AI adoption is highest in finance, healthcare, and manufacturing.
cases.description: Prediction question with estimates and history only
cases.rationale: Estimates and historical patterns don't guarantee future outcomes

cases.query: Why do some startups fail while others succeed?
contexts: 90% of startups fail within the first 5 years according to Bureau of Labor Statistics.
Successful startups like Airbnb and Uber pivoted multiple times before finding product-market fit.
Common characteristics of failed startups include running out of cash and lack of market need.
cases.description: Patterns and correlations but no proven mechanism
cases.rationale: Context lists characteristics associated with failure/success but not proven causes

cases.query: What will Bitcoin's price be in 2025?
contexts: Bitcoin reached an all-time high of $73,000 in March 2024.
Analyst predictions range from $50,000 to $200,000 depending on regulatory developments.
The next Bitcoin halving is expected in April 2024, historically followed by price increases.
cases.description: Prediction question with opinions and patterns only
cases.rationale: Historical patterns and analyst opinions don't guarantee future prices

cases.query: Why do people who exercise regularly earn more money?
contexts: Studies show regular exercisers earn 9% more on average than non-exercisers.
Exercise frequency correlates positively with education level and job seniority.
Gym memberships are most common among professionals aged 25-45.
cases.description: Correlation data without causal mechanism
cases.rationale: Exercise may not cause higher earnings - both could be effects of other factors (education, time availability, wealth)

cases.query: What do users think about the new design?
contexts: We conducted 5 user interviews about the redesign.
3 users said they preferred the new navigation, 2 preferred the old.
Interview participants were selected from our beta tester pool.
cases.description: Very small sample size for generalization
cases.rationale: 5 interviews from beta testers can't represent all users

cases.query: Why did customer churn increase?
contexts: Monthly churn rate increased from 2.1% to 3.8% over six months.
During this period, we raised prices by 15% and launched two new competitors entered the market.
Support ticket volume increased 40% in the same period.
cases.description: Multiple potential causes without attribution
cases.rationale: Price increase, competition, and support issues all occurred - can't determine which caused churn

cases.query: Will the merger be approved by regulators?
contexts: The proposed merger would create a company with 35% market share.
Similar mergers in other industries were approved in 2023.
The regulatory review process typically takes 12-18 months.
cases.description: Regulatory prediction with precedent but no certainty
cases.rationale: Past approvals don't guarantee this one - different circumstances may apply

cases.query: Is remote work better for productivity?
contexts: A Stanford study found 13% productivity increase in remote call center workers.
The study tracked 500 employees over 9 months.
Participants self-selected into the remote work group.
cases.description: Single study with methodological limitations
cases.rationale: One study, specific job type (call center), self-selection bias - can't generalize to all work

cases.query: Why is the team's velocity declining?
contexts: Sprint velocity dropped from 45 points to 32 points over the last 4 sprints.
The team added 2 new members during this period.
Technical debt backlog grew from 20 to 45 items.
The product manager changed in sprint 3.
cases.description: Multiple changes coinciding with velocity drop
cases.rationale: New members, tech debt, and PM change all occurred - can't isolate the cause

cases.query: Why do companies with diverse boards perform better?
contexts: McKinsey found companies in the top quartile for board diversity were 35% more likely to outperform peers.
The study analyzed 1,000 companies across 15 countries.
Diverse boards are more common in larger, more established companies.
cases.description: Correlation between diversity and performance
cases.rationale: Correlation doesn't prove causation - larger companies may have both more diversity AND better performance

cases.query: How many users will we have by year end?
contexts: Current user count is 50,000, up from 30,000 six months ago.
Growth has been approximately 10% month-over-month.
We plan to launch in 3 new markets next quarter.
cases.description: Growth projection with many unknowns
cases.rationale: Past growth rate may not continue - new markets add uncertainty

cases.query: Which framework is better for our project?
contexts: React has 200k GitHub stars, Vue has 200k, Angular has 90k.
Our team has 2 developers with React experience.
The project requires server-side rendering capabilities.
cases.description: Partial information for framework decision
cases.rationale: GitHub stars and team experience don't fully determine best choice - many other factors matter

cases.query: What's the best marketing channel for our product?
contexts: We ran a 2-week test with $1,000 budget split across 3 channels.
Google Ads generated 50 clicks, Facebook 120 clicks, LinkedIn 30 clicks.
We acquired 3 customers total during the test period.
cases.description: Very limited test data for major decision
cases.rationale: 2 weeks, $1K, and 3 customers is insufficient data to determine best channel

cases.query: Why did conversion rate improve after the redesign?
contexts: Conversion rate increased from 2.1% to 2.8% after the homepage redesign.
The redesign launched the same week as a major press mention.
Seasonal traffic typically increases during this period.
cases.description: Improvement coinciding with multiple events
cases.rationale: Redesign, press mention, and seasonality all occurred - can't attribute improvement to redesign alone

cases.query: Why do cities with more ice cream sales have higher crime rates?
contexts: Data shows a strong positive correlation (r=0.85) between ice cream sales and crime rates across US cities.
Both ice cream sales and crime rates peak during summer months.
Cities with populations over 500,000 show the strongest correlation between these variables.
cases.description: Classic confounding variable example
cases.rationale: Ice cream doesn't cause crime - hot weather (confounding variable) increases both

cases.query: Why do children who eat breakfast perform better in school?
contexts: Studies show students who eat breakfast score 17% higher on standardized tests.
Breakfast-eating students have 25% fewer absences and better classroom behavior.
Schools with free breakfast programs see improved academic outcomes across all subjects.
cases.description: Correlation may reflect underlying factors
cases.rationale: Breakfast may be a proxy for stable home environment, parental involvement, or socioeconomic status

cases.query: Why do hospital patients who get more visitors recover faster?
contexts: A study of 2,000 patients found those with daily visitors had 20% shorter hospital stays.
Patients with more visitors reported higher satisfaction scores.
Visitor frequency correlated with patient age and diagnosis severity.
cases.description: Correlation with confounding health factors
cases.rationale: Healthier patients may both recover faster AND have more visitors - correlation not causation

cases.query: Why do people who read more books live longer?
contexts: Yale research found book readers had a 23-month survival advantage over non-readers.
The study controlled for age, race, self-reported health, and employment.
Reading 3.5 hours per week was associated with maximum longevity benefit.
cases.description: Controlled study but causation still uncertain
cases.rationale: Even with controls, reading may be marker for other healthy behaviors not measured

cases.query: Based on our pilot results, should we scale this approach?
contexts: The pilot ran for 3 weeks with 12 participants in one office location.
8 of 12 participants reported positive experiences (67% satisfaction).
Implementation cost was $500 per participant.
We plan to roll out to 5,000 employees across 20 locations.
cases.description: Tiny pilot used to justify massive rollout
cases.rationale: 12 people in 3 weeks in one location cannot predict results across 5,000 people in 20 locations

cases.query: Is this treatment effective?
contexts: A phase 2 trial showed 45% improvement vs placebo in 120 patients.
The trial duration was 8 weeks with follow-up at 12 weeks.
Side effects were reported by 23% of the treatment group vs 18% of placebo.
No phase 3 trials have been completed yet.
cases.description: Promising but incomplete clinical evidence
cases.rationale: Phase 2 results are preliminary - phase 3 trials needed to confirm efficacy and safety

cases.query: Why did our revenue grow 50% this year?
contexts: Revenue grew from $10M to $15M this year.
We hired a new VP of Sales in January who implemented a new sales methodology.
The overall market grew 40% this year due to regulatory tailwinds.
Our largest competitor went out of business in Q2.
We raised prices by 10% in March.
cases.description: Multiple factors contributing to outcome
cases.rationale: New VP, market growth, competitor exit, AND price increase all contributed - can't attribute to single cause

cases.query: Will this technology become mainstream in 5 years?
contexts: Current adoption is at 2% of potential users, up from 0.5% two years ago.
Major tech companies have announced investments in the technology.
Regulatory frameworks are still being developed.
Cost has decreased 60% over the past 3 years but remains 10x higher than alternatives.
cases.description: Early-stage technology prediction
cases.rationale: Rapid growth from tiny base, uncertain regulation, and high cost make prediction unreliable

cases.query: Why do employees who take more vacation days get promoted more often?
contexts: Internal HR data shows employees who take 15+ vacation days are 25% more likely to be promoted.
These employees also have higher performance ratings on average.
Vacation day usage correlates with tenure and seniority level.
cases.description: Correlation confounded by seniority
cases.rationale: Senior employees both take more vacation AND get promoted more - vacation doesn't cause promotions

cases.query: Should we adopt this new methodology based on the case study?
contexts: Company X adopted this methodology and saw 40% efficiency gains.
The case study was published by the methodology's creator.
Company X is a Fortune 500 enterprise; we are a 50-person startup.
The implementation took Company X 18 months with a dedicated team of 12.
cases.description: Single biased case study for major decision
cases.rationale: One case study from the creator, different company size, significant resource requirements - insufficient for confident recommendation

cases.query: Why did our NPS score improve this quarter?
contexts: NPS increased from 32 to 48 this quarter.
We launched a new customer success program in month 1.
We also fixed 15 long-standing bugs reported by customers.
Our main competitor had a major security breach that was widely publicized.
We changed our NPS survey methodology to follow up faster after interactions.
cases.description: Multiple simultaneous changes affecting NPS
cases.rationale: CS program, bug fixes, competitor issues, AND survey changes all occurred - can't isolate which improved NPS

cases.query: What percentage of users will pay for premium?
contexts: In our soft launch, 8 out of 100 users upgraded to premium (8%).
The soft launch ran for 2 weeks in one geographic region.
Users were acquired through a single Facebook ad campaign.
Premium pricing was set at $9.99/month during the test.
cases.description: Limited test used to project conversion
cases.rationale: 100 users from one channel in one region over 2 weeks cannot reliably predict global conversion rates

cases.query: Why do companies that blog more have higher revenue?
contexts: Companies publishing 16+ blog posts per month have 3.5x more traffic than those publishing 0-4.
Higher traffic correlates with higher revenue in B2B SaaS.
Companies with larger marketing teams publish more frequently.
cases.description: Correlation confounded by company size/resources
cases.rationale: Larger companies have more resources for both blogging AND revenue generation - blogging may not cause revenue

cases.query: Will our product succeed in the Japanese market?
contexts: Our product is successful in the US and UK markets.
Japan has the third-largest economy and high smartphone penetration.
70% of mobile app revenue in Japan comes from gaming.
Our product is a productivity app with English-only interface currently.
cases.description: Market entry prediction with cultural gaps
cases.rationale: Success elsewhere, gaming-dominated market, and language barrier make Japanese success uncertain

cases.query: Is our security adequate against sophisticated attackers?
contexts: We passed our annual penetration test with no critical findings.
The pentest was conducted over 5 days by a mid-tier security firm.
We use industry-standard encryption and authentication.
No breaches have occurred in our 3-year history.
cases.description: Security assessment with significant gaps
cases.rationale: 5-day pentest can't find all vulnerabilities; no breaches doesn't mean no vulnerabilities; sophisticated attackers have more resources than mid-tier firms

cases.query: Does intermittent fasting improve cognitive function?
contexts: A 2023 review in Nutritional Neuroscience states: 'Results suggest intermittent fasting may improve certain cognitive markers.'
The review analyzed 12 studies with sample sizes ranging from 20 to 150 participants.
Authors note: 'More rigorous, long-term trials are needed to confirm these preliminary observations.'
cases.description: Source uses hedging language ('may', 'suggest', 'preliminary')
cases.rationale: The source itself hedges with 'suggest', 'may', and 'preliminary' - system should preserve this uncertainty rather than state definitively

cases.query: Is this new cancer treatment effective?
contexts: Early trial results indicate the treatment could be effective for certain patient subgroups.
Lead researcher Dr. Martinez stated: 'Preliminary findings are encouraging, but we cannot draw definitive conclusions yet.'
The Phase 1 trial enrolled 45 patients with a 6-month follow-up period.
cases.description: Medical source explicitly hedges effectiveness claim
cases.rationale: Source uses 'could be', 'preliminary', 'cannot draw definitive conclusions' - these hedges must be preserved in any answer

cases.query: Will autonomous vehicles be mainstream by 2030?
contexts: Industry analysts believe autonomous vehicles are likely to achieve significant market penetration by 2030.
McKinsey report notes: 'Under optimistic assumptions, AVs could represent 10-15% of new vehicle sales.'
Regulatory experts suggest approval timelines remain uncertain in key markets.
cases.description: Prediction sources use hedging throughout
cases.rationale: All sources hedge: 'believe', 'likely', 'could', 'under optimistic assumptions', 'uncertain' - no confident prediction is warranted

cases.query: What causes migraines?
contexts: According to HealthyLivingBlog.com: 'Migraines are caused by electromagnetic radiation from cell phones and WiFi routers.'
The blog post, written by wellness coach Jenny Thompson, has been shared 50,000 times on social media.
The article cites 'numerous studies' but provides no specific references or links.
cases.description: Non-authoritative source making causal claims
cases.rationale: Blog post by non-medical professional, no citations, making definitive causal claims about medical condition - source quality is insufficient for confident answer

cases.query: Is this supplement safe for long-term use?
contexts: A popular health influencer with 2M followers posted: 'I've taken this supplement daily for 3 years with amazing results and zero side effects!'
The post received 15,000 likes and hundreds of comments from followers sharing similar experiences.
The influencer disclosed a paid partnership with the supplement manufacturer.
cases.description: Social media testimonial as safety evidence
cases.rationale: Influencer testimonial with financial conflict of interest, anecdotal evidence, no clinical data - cannot confidently assess long-term safety

cases.query: Is this medication safe for children under 12?
contexts: Clinical trials demonstrated the medication is safe and effective in adults aged 18-65.
The study enrolled 2,500 participants over a 2-year period with comprehensive safety monitoring.
No pediatric trials have been conducted to date.
The FDA approved the medication for adult use only.
cases.description: Adult study applied to pediatric question
cases.rationale: Study population (adults 18-65) doesn't match question population (children under 12) - children metabolize drugs differently, cannot extrapolate safety

cases.query: Will this agile methodology work for our enterprise with 5,000 employees?
contexts: Case study: TechStartup Inc. (25 employees) implemented this methodology and saw 60% faster delivery.
The startup's CTO reported: 'The informal communication and flat structure made adoption seamless.'
Implementation took 2 weeks with the entire team co-located in one office.
cases.description: Startup case study applied to enterprise context
cases.rationale: 25-person co-located startup vs 5,000-employee enterprise - organizational scale, structure, and communication patterns differ fundamentally

cases.query: Will this marketing strategy work in the US market?
contexts: The campaign achieved 300% ROI in South Korea over 6 months.
Key success factors included partnerships with local K-pop influencers and integration with KakaoTalk.
The target demographic was urban millennials aged 25-35 in Seoul metropolitan area.
cases.description: Different country study applied to US question
cases.rationale: South Korean market has different social platforms (KakaoTalk vs US platforms), cultural context (K-pop influence), and consumer behavior - cannot assume transferability

cases.query: What will the electric vehicle market share be in 2026?
contexts: EV market share grew from 2.5% in 2019 to 4.5% in 2020 to 6.5% in 2021 to 8% in 2022.
This represents consistent year-over-year growth of approximately 2 percentage points.
Government incentives remained stable during this period.
Report published: January 2023.
cases.description: Historical trend used for future prediction
cases.rationale: 2019-2022 trend data is 3-4 years old for 2026 prediction - market conditions, competition, regulations, and technology have changed significantly

cases.query: What is the current size of the global AI market?
contexts: According to a comprehensive market analysis, the global AI market was valued at $136.5 billion.
The report projected 35% annual growth rate based on adoption trends.
Key growth drivers identified included healthcare AI and autonomous systems.
Report publication date: March 2022.
cases.description: Outdated market report for 'current' question
cases.rationale: 3-year-old market report cannot answer 'current' market size question - AI market has evolved dramatically since 2022 with ChatGPT launch and subsequent developments

cases.query: How do I use the componentWillMount lifecycle method in React?
contexts: componentWillMount() is invoked immediately before mounting occurs. It is called before render().
Note: This method is considered legacy and you should avoid it in new code. It has been renamed to UNSAFE_componentWillMount.
As of React 16.3, componentWillMount is deprecated. The React team recommends using componentDidMount or the constructor instead.
cases.description: Question about deprecated API that still exists but shouldn't be used
cases.rationale: Context explicitly states the method is deprecated and should be avoided - answer must include this qualification rather than simply explaining usage

cases.query: How do I make HTTP requests using the request library in Node.js?
contexts: The request library provides a simple way to make HTTP calls in Node.js: request('http://example.com', (err, res, body) => { ... })
IMPORTANT: As of February 2020, the request library has been fully deprecated and is in maintenance mode only.
The maintainers recommend migrating to alternatives like node-fetch, axios, or the built-in fetch API (Node 18+).
cases.description: Question about deprecated library that technically still works
cases.rationale: The library is explicitly deprecated - any answer must qualify that users should consider alternatives rather than providing usage instructions without warning

cases.query: What was Apple's revenue last quarter?
contexts: Apple Inc. reported Q4 2024 revenue of $94.9 billion, driven by strong iPhone and Services performance.
Apple Records, the Beatles' record label, announced restructuring plans and reported annual revenue of £12 million.
The European apple (Malus domestica) harvest yielded approximately 12 million tonnes valued at €8 billion.
cases.description: Ambiguous 'Apple' could refer to multiple entities in context
cases.rationale: Context contains information about Apple Inc., Apple Records, and apple fruit - the query is ambiguous and answer should clarify which entity or acknowledge the ambiguity

cases.query: When was the Mercury program completed?
contexts: NASA's Mercury program concluded in 1963 after six crewed flights, paving the way for the Gemini program.
The Mercury automobile program ended in 2011 when Ford discontinued the brand after 72 years of production.
The Mercury Prize for British and Irish albums was established in 1992 and continues annually.
cases.description: Ambiguous 'Mercury program' matches multiple contexts
cases.rationale: Multiple 'Mercury programs' exist - NASA space program vs Ford Mercury car program - answer must clarify which one or acknowledge ambiguity

cases.query: What is the current status of the Paris Agreement?
contexts: The Paris Agreement on climate change, adopted in 2015, has been ratified by 194 parties as of 2024.
The Paris Peace Agreements of 1973 ended direct U.S. military involvement in Vietnam.
The 2024 Paris Agreement on AI Safety was signed by 28 nations and establishes voluntary guidelines for AI development.
cases.description: Multiple 'Paris Agreements' exist across different domains
cases.rationale: Context mentions climate agreement, Vietnam peace agreement, and AI safety agreement - query doesn't specify which Paris Agreement

cases.query: What is the budget for the project?
contexts: Project Alpha (Marketing): Q1 budget allocation of $250,000 for digital advertising campaigns.
Project Beta (Engineering): Annual budget of $1.2 million for infrastructure modernization.
Project Gamma (Research): Multi-year funding of $5 million for advanced materials development.
All projects are currently active and within their respective budget constraints.
cases.description: Ambiguous 'the project' when multiple projects exist
cases.rationale: Three different projects with different budgets are mentioned - cannot determine which 'the project' refers to without clarification

cases.query: When is the deadline?
contexts: Phase 1 deliverables are due by March 15, 2025.
The grant application deadline is April 30, 2025.
Final project completion is scheduled for December 31, 2025.
All milestones are on track according to the latest status report.
cases.description: Ambiguous 'the deadline' when multiple deadlines exist
cases.rationale: Context contains three different deadlines - Phase 1, grant application, and final completion - query doesn't specify which deadline

cases.query: Who is the team lead?
contexts: Sarah Chen leads the frontend development team with 8 engineers.
Marcus Williams is the team lead for backend services, overseeing 12 developers.
Dr. Emily Rodriguez heads the data science team of 5 researchers.
Cross-functional coordination happens through weekly sync meetings.
cases.description: Ambiguous 'the team' when multiple teams exist
cases.rationale: Three different teams with three different leads are mentioned - cannot determine which team the question refers to

cases.query: What is the current price?
contexts: As of January 2024, the standard tier was priced at $29/month.
The March 2024 price adjustment set the rate at $35/month.
Our October 2024 promotional pricing offers 20% off the regular price.
Pricing is subject to change based on market conditions.
cases.description: Multiple 'current' timeframes with different prices
cases.rationale: Context shows prices from different times in 2024 - 'current' is ambiguous without knowing today's date relative to these entries

cases.query: What is the latest version?
contexts: Version 4.2 was released on June 15, 2024 with performance improvements.
The beta channel currently offers version 5.0-beta.3 with new features.
Long-term support (LTS) users should use version 3.8.12, updated August 2024.
Version numbering follows semantic versioning principles.
cases.description: Ambiguous 'latest' depends on release channel
cases.rationale: Multiple 'latest' versions exist depending on channel (stable, beta, LTS) - query doesn't specify which context

cases.query: What is the system's performance?
contexts: Response latency averages 45ms at the 95th percentile under normal load.
The accuracy rate for classification tasks reached 97.3% on the benchmark dataset.
Operating costs decreased to $0.002 per transaction after optimization.
System uptime has been maintained at 99.95% over the past year.
cases.description: Ambiguous 'performance' could mean speed, accuracy, cost, or reliability
cases.rationale: Context provides multiple performance metrics - latency, accuracy, cost, uptime - 'performance' is ambiguous without specifying which dimension

cases.query: How efficient is the process?
contexts: Time efficiency: The automated process completes in 2.3 hours vs 8 hours manual.
Cost efficiency: Processing cost reduced from $15 to $4 per unit.
Energy efficiency: Power consumption is 340 kWh per 1000 units processed.
Labor efficiency: One operator can now manage 5 production lines instead of 2.
cases.description: Ambiguous 'efficiency' has multiple dimensions in context
cases.rationale: Four different efficiency metrics are provided - time, cost, energy, labor - cannot determine which type of efficiency the question asks about

cases.query: Why did our customer acquisition cost decrease by 35%?
contexts: Customer acquisition cost dropped from $150 to $97 over the past quarter.
During this period, we launched a referral program that generated 2,000 new signups.
We also reduced our paid advertising spend by 40% as an experiment.
A viral TikTok video about our product reached 5 million views organically.
Our main competitor raised their prices by 25%, driving comparison shoppers to us.
cases.description: Four simultaneous changes make attribution impossible
cases.rationale: Referral program, reduced ad spend, viral video, and competitor price increase all happened - cannot isolate which caused the CAC decrease

cases.query: What caused the website conversion rate to double?
contexts: Conversion rate increased from 2.1% to 4.3% over three months.
We redesigned the checkout flow to reduce steps from 5 to 3.
Page load time improved from 4.2 seconds to 1.8 seconds after infrastructure upgrades.
We introduced a limited-time 20% discount promotion during this period.
Mobile traffic increased from 40% to 65% of total visitors.
cases.description: Multiple simultaneous improvements obscure causation
cases.rationale: Checkout redesign, faster loading, discount promotion, and traffic mix change all occurred - each could explain the improvement

cases.query: Does having a mentor accelerate career advancement?
contexts: Employees with mentors are promoted 5x more frequently than those without mentors.
Mentored employees report 25% higher job satisfaction scores.
High-potential employees identified in leadership programs are assigned executive mentors.
The mentorship program targets employees already on the fast-track for promotion.
cases.description: Causation could flow in either direction
cases.rationale: Do mentors cause promotions, or are promotion-track employees assigned mentors? Selection bias makes causation direction unclear

cases.query: Does exercise improve mental health?
contexts: People who exercise regularly report 40% lower rates of depression and anxiety.
A survey found that gym members score higher on mental well-being assessments.
Individuals with depression are less likely to engage in physical activity.
Mental health conditions often manifest as fatigue and reduced motivation for exercise.
cases.description: Bidirectional causation makes simple answer impossible
cases.rationale: Does exercise improve mental health, or does good mental health enable exercise? Both directions are plausible from this evidence

cases.query: Did the price increase cause customers to churn?
contexts: Customer churn increased significantly during Q3 2024.
We implemented a 15% price increase effective July 1, 2024.
A major competitor launched an aggressive discount campaign in Q3.
Our support team experienced a 3-week backlog due to understaffing in the same period.
All three events occurred within the same quarter.
cases.description: Multiple events in same period make sequencing unclear
cases.rationale: Price increase, competitor campaign, and support issues all happened in Q3 - cannot determine which caused churn or if they interacted

cases.query: Is hormone replacement therapy safe for menopausal women?
contexts: For decades, HRT was considered safe and widely prescribed for menopausal symptoms.
The 2002 Women's Health Initiative study found increased risks of breast cancer and heart disease with HRT.
Post-WHI reanalysis suggested the risks were primarily in women starting HRT later in life.
Current guidelines distinguish between different types of HRT and patient age at initiation.
The medical consensus on HRT safety has evolved significantly over the past 20 years.
cases.description: Medical consensus changed dramatically over time
cases.rationale: Initial confidence in safety was overturned, then partially restored with nuance - answer requires acknowledging this evolution and current complexity
